label: Manifold
dominant_mnemonic: A curved patch that is locally ordinary
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to one curved blue patch, one point p, and a small local neighbourhood cue.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a smooth curved manifold patch with intrinsic grid curves, a highlighted point p, and a small local neighbourhood around p. The graphic should say that the space may be globally curved but locally chartable.
physics_idea: A manifold is the smooth setting for spaces that look locally like ordinary coordinate space without yet specifying distances or times.
avoid: Metric grids, curvature tensors, global coordinate axes, or treating the whole manifold as a flat plane.
icon_caption: A curved patch with one point p suggests a space that is locally ordinary.
detail_caption: The manifold patch may be globally curved, but near p it has a small local neighbourhood suitable for coordinates.

label: Coordinate chart
dominant_mnemonic: A local patch mapped to coordinate numbers
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a manifold patch, a flat coordinate rectangle, and one map arrow phi.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a local region U on a manifold mapped by phi to a flat coordinate plane with axes and grid. Show the same point on both sides to make clear that coordinates are labels for manifold points.
physics_idea: A coordinate chart assigns numbers to points in a local region of a manifold.
avoid: A global coordinate system covering everything, metric distances, or making the coordinate plane more physical than the manifold.
icon_caption: A patch is mapped by phi to coordinate labels x^mu.
detail_caption: A chart maps a local manifold patch to coordinate numbers; the red point is the same point before and after labelling.

label: Coordinate transformation
dominant_mnemonic: Same point with two coordinate labels
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to two coordinate grids connected by a transformation arrow and one matching red point.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as two local coordinate grids with the same point shown in both. A clean arrow labelled x'(x) should indicate relabelling between coordinate descriptions, not motion of the physical point.
physics_idea: A coordinate transformation changes labels assigned to the same manifold point.
avoid: Moving the point as a physical displacement, global inertial frames only, metric distances, or tensor transformation laws as the main motif.
icon_caption: Two coordinate grids label the same point in different ways.
detail_caption: A coordinate transformation relabels the same point; the red dashed cue connects descriptions rather than moving the point.

label: Worldline
dominant_mnemonic: A curve of events through spacetime
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to x/ct axes, a blue curve, and a few red event dots.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a spacetime coordinate plot with a future-directed curve passing through event dots. Add a few tick marks or labels only in the detail view so the path reads as a history through spacetime.
physics_idea: A worldline is the spacetime history of a particle, observer, clock, detector, or light signal.
avoid: A spatial trajectory at one time, force arrows, metric curvature as the main subject, or a curve that looks exactly lightlike unless light is the topic.
icon_caption: A blue curve through red events represents a worldline.
detail_caption: A worldline is a curve of events through spacetime; the coordinate plot is only one way to draw that curve.

label: Tangent space
dominant_mnemonic: A flat vector space attached at one point
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a curved patch, one point p, and a tilted tangent plane with basis arrows.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a tangent plane attached at p on a curved manifold patch. Add two green basis directions within the plane and keep the connector to p visible so the plane reads as attached at that point.
physics_idea: The tangent space is the local vector space attached to a manifold point.
avoid: A free-floating plane detached from p, global coordinate axes, or guide axes that look fixed to the screen instead of lying in the tangent plane.
icon_caption: A flat tangent plane is attached to the curved manifold at p.
detail_caption: For this two-dimensional manifold the tangent space \(T_pM\) is a two-dimensional local vector space at \(p\); its basis directions live in the attached plane.

label: Cotangent space
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a tangent-plane motif with amber covector/gradient stripes and T_p^*.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a tangent-plane-like local space with a family of amber level lines and a covector arrow crossing them. Pair visually with tangent space while making the dual/covector role distinct.
physics_idea: The cotangent space contains covectors or one-forms that act on tangent vectors to produce numbers.
avoid: Treating covectors as just ordinary arrows, metric raising/lowering as already assumed, dense differential-form notation, or standalone algebra detached from the point p.
icon_caption: Amber level lines and a covector arrow suggest the dual space T_p^*.
detail_caption: Cotangent vectors act on tangent directions; the graphic uses a gradient-like motif to show the dual partner of tangent space.

label: Tensor field
dominant_mnemonic: Tensor objects assigned point by point
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a manifold patch with several small T glyphs attached at different points.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a curved manifold patch carrying several compact tensor glyphs. The glyphs should be placed at different points so the viewer sees a field as an assignment over the manifold rather than one isolated tensor.
physics_idea: A tensor field assigns tensor objects smoothly to points of a manifold.
avoid: A single standalone tensor matrix, particle trajectories, or making the tensor field look like one global object detached from the manifold.
icon_caption: Several T glyphs on the patch show a tensor assigned at each point.
detail_caption: A tensor field is not one isolated tensor; it is a smoothly varying tensor assignment across the manifold.

label: Abstract and component indices
dominant_mnemonic: One tensor shown abstractly and in a chosen basis
icon_design: Show T with abstract indices beside a small component matrix.
detail_design: Contrast an abstract tensor symbol with its component array and label the two descriptions. Emphasize that a basis produces components without changing the tensor.
physics_idea: Abstract indices describe tensor type while component indices label numbers in a chosen basis.
avoid: Treating abstract indices as numerical labels or showing unrelated tensors.
icon_caption: An abstract T and a component matrix depict two descriptions of one tensor.
detail_caption: Components depend on a chosen basis; the abstract tensor does not.

label: Tensor transformation law
icon_design: Show two component grids T and T-prime connected by a Lambda arrow.
detail_design: Draw two coordinate-component arrays linked by a transformation Lambda. State that components change while the tensor remains the same geometric object.
physics_idea: The tensor transformation law preserves the geometric tensor while changing its coordinate components.
avoid: Physical deformation, motion of the object, or a scalar with no index transformation.
icon_caption: Lambda maps one component grid to another.
detail_caption: The component arrays change between coordinates, but they represent the same tensor.
